findings.evidence: Use for asking for a raise, salary, promotion or workload terms; delivering a layoff... Not for feedback on a specific behavior... or feedback recaps (use feedback-mastery)
findings.fix: Prepare, rehearse and follow up on high-stakes workplace conversations where the outcome is negotiated, facts are disputed, the news is bad, or emotions may derail it. Use when asking for a raise, salary, promotion or workload terms; delivering a layoff, role elimination or other bad news; handling a clash after public criticism or a blowup; mediating a dispute between others whose accounts of the facts conflict; raising a sensitive personal concern (health, family), harassment, or threats at work; deciding whether you are calm enough to talk; or repairing after getting defensive, even if the user never says 'difficult conversation', '1:1' or 'mediation'. Not for feedback on a specific behavior (including to each person in a conflict you lead), recognition, replying to vague criticism, scope or deadline pushback, or feedback recaps (use feedback-mastery); not for legal advice, drafting formal complaints, PIPs, ratings, policy, or company-wide announcements.
